author: thomas
text: This money is going to be the down payment on a home next summer. Even a small drop at the time I withdraw it would be a problem for me.

author: thomas
text: I am considering investments for the next five years. I prefer a regular income and I can accept small variations.

author: thomas
text: My horizon is eight years. I want growth but I would keep part of it stable. A temporary 12% drop would not make me sell.

author: thomas
text: These savings are for in fifteen years at least. I am mainly looking for long-term growth, even with a 35% drop along the way.

author: thomas
text: I would like a good return, but I must preserve the capital. I might need the money in a few months.

author: thomas
text: I will leave the money invested for at least ten years. I accept sharp drawdowns and would keep investing after a 30% loss to pursue growth.

author: thomas
text: I do not need the money for a few years. I can handle some fluctuations, but a significant loss would keep me awake at night. Stability comes first.

author: thomas
text: I want a balanced portfolio over seven years. I can take moderate losses, but I would reduce my positions if the risk became too high.

author: thomas
text: I am just starting out and I would like to understand the options. I do not yet know my horizon or the losses I could bear.

author: thomas
text: No withdrawal planned for twenty years. Long-term return is my priority. Even after large drops, I would keep my investments.
